facts: Goal: post several jobs a week, reusing the wording of older posts.
Vocabulary: "reqs" and "the hiring manager", not "positions" or "owners".
Objection: losing a draft, so descriptions are often written elsewhere first.
Objection: finding out only after publishing that a hiring manager has no account.
Tool: a text file of descriptions beside the form, and a spreadsheet of who is waiting on what.
remarks: I write the description somewhere else first, because I have lost a whole draft to a form before.
If the hiring manager has no account yet, I need to know before I press publish, not after.
Every req has a budget code, and if the form hides that field I go looking for it.
We still track who is waiting on what in a spreadsheet, whatever the tool says.

facts: Goal: read a resume and leave a decision within a minute.
Vocabulary: "shortlist" and "pass"; few know what a pipeline stage is called in the product.
Objection: not knowing whether a decision or feedback was saved or seen.
Tool: the email that brings them in, often read on a phone, and messages to the recruiter.
remarks: I open it from the email on my phone, read the resume, and I want to be done before my next meeting.
Tell me whose turn it is, because I only come here when someone asks me to.
I wrote two paragraphs of feedback once and I still do not know if anyone saw them.
If I cannot tell whether my decision saved, I send the recruiter a message instead.

facts: Goal: set the tool up once and return when a person, a rule or an audit changes something.
Objection: the wrong person getting access matters more than speed.
Tool: settings pages, which they read closely.
remarks: I need to see who can approve a job before I invite anyone else.
I invited a manager last week and I cannot tell whether the invite ever arrived.
Changing a setting should say who it affects, because I answer for it in the audit.

facts: Goal: check what is waiting for a review each morning across every open job.
Objection: a list that hides closed jobs without saying so.
Tool: chat to chase people, and their own notes.
remarks: I start every morning by asking which candidates have been waiting the longest.
I do not own any of these jobs, I just keep them moving.
When the list hides closed jobs I can never tell if a job is gone or just filtered out.
